objective: Keep long VLM stages visibly alive and honest instead of appearing frozen at a fixed percentage, while preserving the existing inference, state, candidate, truth, and training contracts.

behavior: VLM discovery, retry, and description phases advance smoothly from their established stage floor toward a bounded 20 percent ceiling using the measured 16 second 4090 baseline.
VLM observation and background refinement advance smoothly toward a bounded 72 percent ceiling using the measured 34 second multi-image baseline.
In-phase interpolation is capped at 92 percent of its allowed range, so waiting cannot falsely cross into the next stage.
Running percentages are explicitly prefixed with the Chinese approximation marker rather than presented as exact completion.
The detail line displays both actual phase elapsed time and the current 4090 typical duration.
The existing task high-water mark still prevents transient retries from moving progress backward; a new task resets it.
Unknown queue time in vlm_waiting remains indeterminate and is not assigned a fabricated duration.

measured_baselines.boundary: These values drive an explicitly approximate UI indicator. They are not a latency SLA or a claim that every request finishes by that time.

acceleration_capacity_audit.decision: Do not disrupt occupied 5090 workloads and do not install an unvalidated heavy engine into the stable 4090 environment.

storage.warning: The Windows system volume remains below the existing 2 GiB advisory threshold. LabelAgent runtime temp remains isolated on D:, but this UI change does not claim Windows-wide storage stability.

boundary: This improves live progress transparency and perceived responsiveness; it does not reduce the underlying 15 to 34 second VLM compute time, prove cross-dataset accuracy, improve slope IoU, or constitute SAM/VLM fine-tuning.
